simple: The short name a program uses to look up the settings for the GPU it found.
analogy: The name on the door of a hall, used to find that hall's sheet of table sizes.
precise: In MP4, the AMD target name taken from hipDeviceProp_t::gcnArchName up to the first colon, or sm_XY built from major and minor on HIP's NVIDIA path, where the installed HIP 5.7 headers do not fill gcnArchName.
source: H1 and R1 of MP4 (HIP 5.7 headers read in this build; suite run)

simple: If the program meets a GPU it has no settings for, it stops and says so instead of guessing.
analogy: A helper who finds no sheet for this hall asks, instead of using another hall's sheet.
precise: Run-time selection of a kernel instance from a table keyed by device key, in which a missing key, a wave width that differs from the table, or an LDS need above the device limit ends the program with an error naming the problem; there is no default row.
source: R1 of MP4 (suite run); course definition

simple: The final document that says, kernel by kernel, how close you came to each vendor's library on each GPU, and why.
analogy: One table comparing your recipe card with each building's master team.
precise: The MP4 deliverable: each kernel's percentage of the vendor library on both GPUs, with reasons, generated from raw benchmark records, every number labelled with GPU, driver and toolkit versions and every reason tagged with evidence (guide 11.6; curriculum E9).
source: C1, C2 of MP4 (guide 11.6 and curriculum E9, pending verification of the cited vendor documents)

simple: How much worse your kernel does, relative to the vendor library, on one GPU than on the other.
analogy: The card is nearly as good as the master team in one building but much further behind in the other.
precise: For a kernel and size, the difference in percentage points between its percentage of the vendor library on the NVIDIA GPU and on the AMD GPU; it compares two ratios with different denominators and says nothing about which GPU is faster.

simple: A short fingerprint of the target numbers, written down when reviewers approve them, so any later change shows.
analogy: The inspector's stamp on the plan, which no longer matches if someone redraws a wall.
precise: The first 16 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the targets, recorded at gate R1; MP4's report generator warns whenever the current targets do not match it (curriculum 13.4: targets are never lowered without the owner's approval and a log entry).

simple: One instruction that does two single-precision multiply-adds at once.
analogy: One helper stirring two pots with two hands in one movement.
precise: v_pk_fma_f32, emitted by the compiler for gfx90a and gfx942 in this build next to scalar v_fmac_f32; its operand pairs indicate two FP32 lanes of work per instruction (the ISA guide's definition is pending verification).
source: R3 of MP4 (compiler output); D3 title only, pending verification

simple: On the newer AMD design, two simple instructions written on one line that are issued together.
analogy: Two helpers in a row given one combined instruction.
precise: An assembly line of the form 'v_dual_fmac_f32 ... :: v_dual_fmac_f32 ...', emitted for gfx1100 in this build; when pairing is allowed is defined in the RDNA3 ISA guide (pending verification). Instruction counts on gfx11 must count both halves.
source: R3 of MP4 (compiler output); D3 title only, pending verification

simple: How many times an instruction appears in the compiled program text, not how often it runs.
analogy: Counting the steps written on the card, not the steps the helpers actually did.
precise: A count over the assembly of one kernel; it equals the work per loop iteration only when the loop body is fully unrolled, and is a check of code generation, not a performance measurement (dynamic counts come from a profiler).

simple: A test that fails when your copy of something no longer matches the original.
analogy: Comparing your copy of the master card with the original before every service.
precise: An automated comparison between data copied from another component (in MP4, MP3's shape matrix) and its source, run with the lab so that the copy cannot silently diverge.
source: R8 of MP4 (mp3_sync run); course definition
